passages.where: At the first marriage the narrator draws a lasting conclusion: a man leaves his father and mother and holds fast to his wife. The note says this answers the not good of being alone in every generation. Leaving home is not a failure of the family God made; it is written into it from the start.

At a wedding in Cana the wine runs out, and Mary tells her grown son. The site's note says she states the need and leaves the response to him, and when he answers that his hour has not yet come, she tells the servants to do whatever he says. A mother brings a concern to her adult son and then lets him act in his own way.

Naomi, widowed and bereaved of both sons, tells her two daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers' homes, and she blesses them with the LORD's kindness and rest. She does not hold them by need, though she needs them badly. One goes and one stays, and Naomi's blessing covers both choices.

Rebekah overhears Isaac and tells her grown son Jacob to do exactly as she says. The note points out that she plans every step and Jacob's part is to obey. The deception that follows splits the family for twenty years. Scripture records a parent running an adult child's life, and what it cost.

Samuel, a faithful prophet raised in God's house, appoints his sons as judges in his old age, and they take bribes and pervert justice. The Bible does not explain it or blame him for it. A godly parent can have grown children who do not walk in his ways.

The elder writes to his friend Gaius that he has no greater joy than to hear that his children are walking in the truth. He means his children in the faith, and the joy is a parent's joy. It comes by hearing, at a distance, of a life lived well that he no longer directs.

The father of a righteous son rejoices, and the son is told to let his father and mother be glad. The same passage asks the grown child not to despise a mother when she is old. Honor and delight run in both directions between parents and grown children.

Grandchildren are the crown of the old, and a father is the glory of his children. The proverb sees a family across three generations. A parent's role does not end when children leave; it changes shape, and often becomes a crown.

Old and ill, Jacob blesses Joseph by blessing Joseph's sons, naming the God who had been his shepherd all his life. The note says he crosses his hands and puts his right hand on the younger, and Genesis shows again that God's blessing is a gift, not a right of rank. The last work of a parent in Genesis is often a blessing spoken over grown children and grandchildren.

God gives Aaron the words to speak over Israel: the LORD bless you and keep you, make his face shine on you, and give you peace. So the priests put God's name on his people. Many parents have spoken these words over grown children, asking for them what a parent can no longer give.

misread.taken: Honor your father and mother is sometimes used by parents to claim a say over an adult child's marriage, work, money or faith, as if the commandment meant obedience for life and disagreement were dishonor.
misread.says: The commandment is given to the whole people, adults included, and Scripture shows what honor means: respect, gratitude and care, including practical support in old age, as the site's notes on 1 Timothy 5 and Mark 7 point out. The obedience Paul asks of children in Ephesians 6 is asked of children in the home, and in the Lord. Genesis 2 says a grown son leaves his father and mother. An adult child can honor a parent and still make his own choices before God; the commandment asks for honor, not control.

whole: There is no ceremony for the day a parent stops steering. It happens in pieces: a decision you were not asked about, a holiday spent with the other family, a career or a city or a spouse you would not have chosen. For many parents the hardest part is not the distance but the silence about faith, a grown child who no longer prays or goes to church, or who believes differently. Others carry the opposite weight, a grown child who cannot leave, or who comes back in crisis. And many parents are quietly grieving the end of the years when they were needed every day.

Scripture expects the change. From the second chapter of Genesis a son leaves his father and mother, and the Bible shows what happens when parents will not let go: Rebekah ran her grown son's life and split her family for twenty years. It is also honest that faithful parents can raise children who go another way. Samuel's sons took bribes, and the text does not blame Samuel or explain it. Most of the pain in this season comes from a love that has not yet changed its form, and from a fear, which most of us share, that if we are not in control, no one is.

So the Bible's wisdom is to move from steering to blessing. Mary at Cana is a quiet model: she named the need to her grown son and then stepped back and told others to do what he said. Naomi blessed her daughters-in-law to go and meant it. Offer counsel when it is asked for and sometimes once when it is not, then leave it. Keep the door open, the table set and the phone answered, without making love conditional on agreement. Honor your grown child's marriage, which comes before you now. Help with money or a place to stay in ways that strengthen them rather than keep them dependent, and say no when a yes would harm them. And pray, which is the one form of influence that does not shrink as they grow.

Underneath it is a trust that each child belongs first to God. The elder's greatest joy was to hear that his children walked in the truth, and he heard it from far away. Jacob's last act was to bless, naming the God who had shepherded him all his life. A parent of grown children can still do that: speak the old blessing over them, the LORD bless you and keep you, and trust the God who keeps them when they are out of sight. The love does not end. It becomes an open hand.
sit: What would it sound like to bless your grown child this month, in words or in a choice, without attaching advice to it?

prayer.lead: The end of a psalm about a household, asking to see your children's children and peace on God's people.
